Silhouette: Four-legged brown bear frame. Host frame: the brown bear sets the outline, body size and overall frame. A single creature that combines a european rhinoceros beetle and a brown bear. Head of the brown bear, fully visible and uncluttered, with clear, discernible eyes. Details: brown bear body and legs, with its own dense fur everywhere else, plain coat, no stripes or spots; from the european rhinoceros beetle, as parts and materials on the brown bear's own body: a head horn grown from the frontal bone of the head, above and between the eyes: smooth, glossy dark cuticle, one horn curving upward and back from the head. Coat texture and patches follow the body outline. Declared fiction: arthropod parts at large size, shown with thick supporting legs and visible breathing openings along the flanks. Bilaterally symmetrical, recognizable limbs, visible sense organs. Habitat cue (forest): dark back and light belly (mild countershading). Prosaic detail: natural lighting, feet in firm contact with the ground with a soft shadow, normal wear on hooves, claws and skin. One creature, full body, side three-quarter view, plain light background, natural history illustration.
Aspect ratio: 1:1.

**Drafting hybrid bear prompt**
I'm composing a detailed natural-history illustration prompt that merges the two reference images, specifying a brown bear with a horned head, spiracles along the flanks, bear legs with claws, and a dark back with light belly in a side three-quarter view.
**Refining spiracle details**
